title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Price increase (2.4%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose to $3.85 (vs $3.76) in 2026-04-06; sales were 6.0 (1.03x baseline), suggesting near-neutral effect. But price hikes generally reduce demand; historical promotion data shows strong price sensitivity. One prior observation at this price, so shrink effect.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 5.8. No event or promotion is scheduled for the target week. The price increased by 2.4% to $3.85, which is above the regular $3.76. Historical data shows that price increases typically suppress demand; past promotions (25–30% off) boosted sales 2–5.7x, but this week has a price hike, not a discount. The only relevant past price change was in 2026-04-06, when the same price ($3.85) was set and sales were 6.0 (1.03x baseline), suggesting minimal lift. With no promotion and no event, and a price increase, demand is likely to be slightly lower. Evidence is thin (one prior week at this price), so shrink toward 1.0. No driver justifies moving the median significantly.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 5.8 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 15.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 12.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-73% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
